Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks great. As we map commercial terms back to teams, two questions came up from Ops and Procurement:

Lena

Lena — thanks, great questions. Attaching a short proposal (Redwood_SLA_proposal_v3.pdf) that covers two packaging options and a suggested retainer model. High level:

- Blended uptime: we can offer a blended uptime commitment across your US + EU footprint. Pricing is typically +5-8% over single-region SLA because of multi-region readiness and failover testing. We show two bands (99.9 blended, 99.95 blended) with corresponding credits.

- Rapid escalation retainer: two tracks — "On-Demand Retainer" (month-to-month) and "Committed Retainer" (12-month discounted commit). Committed retainer gets a tiered discount tied to annual commit (5% at $X/month, 10% at $Y/month).

I'll put together a one-page option matrix for Finance and loop Jordan and Kim for input on pricing floor + operational constraints.

Would you and Matt be available for a 30-min sync on Thursday?

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: Fwd: SLA packaging question and retainer economics — pricing request (internal)

Team — forwarding ClearWave's ask. Key asks: blended uptime across US/EU and retainer economics with stepped discounts for a 12-month commit. Drafted two options in the attached PDF. Need quick guidance on:

1) Discount band we can offer for a mid-market account (ClearWave is target ~$1.2M ARR potential next 12 months) — I was thinking 8–10% max on committed retainer if they take a 12-month commit and a 6% uplift for blended 99.95 vs 99.9. Thoughts?

2) Operational guardrails: how many on-call hours/days are included under the retainer and how do we limit runbook work so this is predictable for our SRE ops? We should call out a "booked hours" monthly cap and a pre-agreed playbook list; additional execution billed at T&M.

3) Any escalation headcount we need to pre-assign for guaranteed response within the retainer window?

Proposed quick offer to present to Finance:
- Option A (Conservative): Blended 99.9 SLA, On-Demand Retainer at $7,500/mo, Committed Retainer (12mo) $6,750/mo (10% discount) includes up to 40 hours/month of runbook execution and two 4-hr guaranteed triage windows per month.
- Option B (Aggressive): Blended 99.95 SLA (+6% uplift), Committed Retainer $11,000/mo (10% discount at 12mo threshold) includes up to 80 hours/month, 24/7 initial triage for P1 incidents (first 2 hours guaranteed), and escalation POC.

Kim, Jordan, Marissa — please reply with redlines inline so I can finalize. Need this back to ClearWave by EOD Thursday.

— Dylan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA packaging question and retainer economics — pricing request (internal)

Thanks Dylan — quick notes inline and below. High level: agree with structure, but we should cap discounts and add clear escalation runbook limits. Suggested edits: 

- Discounting: we can approve up to 10% on the committed retainer at $1.2M+ annualized TCV but require a non-refundable 30% initial payment on signing (amortized against first 3 months). If they want deeper discounting, escalate to Sales Ops/Rev.

- Blended SLA uplift: 99.95 blended at +6% is reasonable. For 99.9 blended we should not charge extra (base).

- Retainer operational limits: commit includes monthly "playbook hours" (Option A: 40h, Option B: 80h). Any execution beyond those hours billed at $250/hr (T&M). For P1 triage we will provide 2 guaranteed initial triage windows per month under Option A, 24/7 rapid triage under Option B (first 2 hours escalation included).

- Escalation staffing: require a named escalation POC and on-call roster; if ClearWave wants guaranteed named SREs for the retainer, that is an add-on at $X/annum.

- Contractual items: include a 30-day pilot clause (reduced retainer at 50% for first 30 days) if they sign within 14 days of proposal, to help close.

If you're OK, I'll sign off on this version and we can present as "Option A (Standard) / Option B (Enhanced)" with the financial table.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
